transcript_facts.fact: Started sertraline about four weeks ago.
Mood is not great, maybe a tiny bit better in the mornings, but mostly the same.
Feeling low since the summer, about three months.
Mood on a scale of 0-10 is three, maybe, some days two.
Sleeping badly, wakes at four and just lies there.
Not really eating, lost about half a stone.
Works as a warehouse supervisor and is signed off for another two weeks.
Reports passive suicidal ideation (easier if I just didn't wake up) most days for the last couple of weeks.
No active suicidal thoughts or plans, wouldn't do anything.
No plans or preparations, like getting hold of tablets.
Protective factors are nephew and mother; couldn't do that to them.
No previous self-harm or suicide attempts.
Drinking about four pints a week.
Correction: Alcohol consumption is four a night, not four pints a week.
Most nights, four cans, sometimes more at the weekend.
Had a bit of nausea the first week of sertraline, which is now gone.
Taking sertraline every morning at 50 milligrams.
Examination findings: looks tired, reduced eye contact, and speech is a bit slow, but talking clearly and making sense.
No sign of anything like hearing voices.
PHQ-9 score today is 19.
Depression is still moderately severe after four weeks with only a small improvement.
Plan to increase sertraline to 100 milligrams once a day.
Plan to refer to the talking therapies service and provide self-referral details.
Plan to get the community mental health crisis team to know about the patient.
Plan to see the patient again in one week, not four.
Safety plan: If thoughts get stronger or acting on them, call NHS 111 (mental health option) or Samaritans on 116 123.
Safety plan: If unable to keep self safe, call 999 or go to A&E.
Clinician asks if patient is willing to keep stockpiled medicines out of the house or have sister look after them.
Patient agrees to keep stockpiled medicines out of the house.
Plan to cut down alcohol gradually and provide details for the local alcohol support service.
